name: Baroque Mythological Sky
description: High-baroque manner — long diagonal compositions, billowing drapery in crimson, gold and slate, strong chiaroscuro, painted as oil on canvas or as fresco.
style_bible: High-baroque painting in the manner of grand ceiling and altarpiece decoration rather than after any named painter — worked as oil on a coarse primed canvas or as fresco on lime plaster, always painted and never photographed. Ground and surface: the canvas weave or the plaster tooth shows through the thinner darks, the paint is laid warm over a russet ground, faces and hands are built in soft blended half-tones with a loaded impasto only on the brightest turn of a cheekbone or a fold of cloth, and the whole surface carries a fine craquelure under a warm varnish bloom. Composition: everything moves on a long diagonal. Where the scene includes figures, they are arranged in a rising or falling sweep from one lower corner toward the opposite upper corner, foreshortened as though seen from below, with limbs and drapery crossing the diagonal to hold the eye inside the frame; nothing is centred, nothing is symmetrical, and no figure stands square to the viewer. Atmosphere: where the scene gives open air or cloud, soft billowing masses may fill the upper field, dense and lit at the top and dissolving into slate and violet shadow beneath, their edges soft enough for a form to pass through. Drapery: any cloth in the scene is painted with sculptural weight — a broad lit face, a deep shadow trough and a warm reflected light at the return — and is never still or neatly arranged. Palette: warm flesh tones where skin is visible — cream, rose and umber — carried against a field that is either stormy in slate, bruised violet and grey-green, or gilded in amber, honey and pale gold. Crimson and gold are the only fully saturated notes; the darks are warm browns rather than black, and the whites are linen and warm grey rather than paper. Light: strong chiaroscuro from one high direction, so one side of every figure is fully lit and the other falls into a warm shadow that keeps its colour; a shaft or opening of brighter tone sits behind the principal form, and the darkest mass of the picture is placed against it. Figures and attendants: where figures appear, they are built heavy and physical and fully draped from the neck to the ankle so that only faces, hands and feet are ever uncovered — there is no nudity anywhere in this look, no bare torso and no bare shoulder, and the weight of a body is read through the fall of cloth rather than through skin. Any further figures stay subordinate and are never the subject; a picture may leave them out entirely. Attributes: any held object stays plainly readable at small size and is drawn as a real object rather than as a symbol floating free. Mood: elevated, weightless, unhurried, and calm even in motion; this look is used for long quiet narration, so the drama sits in the composition and the light rather than in a face. Keep the contract content-independent: no named deity, no fixed episode, no insignia, no wordmark and no copied composition.
